about: The client's own copy of the character being created, the one the creation window edits and the client sends whole to the server on the window's next change. A look, a name, abilities and a voice written into its Definition reach the server's CharacterDefinition with that message and land on the created character.

evidence.says: Script Extender exposes it as ClientCCBaseDefinitionState with the field Definition (Definition, Visual, Name, Abilities, LevelUpData)

in SYS_CC_I, Visual (7 Visuals, 9 Elements, colours), Name, Abilities and Definition.Voice written on the client, then the window's command ChangeCharacterName run: the server's CCCharacterDefinition.Definition read all of them back, and after FinishCreating the player in TUT_Avernus_C carried them in CharacterCreationAppearance, CharacterCreationStats and Voice
Script Extender's header Components/CharacterCreation.h binds ClientCCBaseDefinitionState to this engine name with the one member Definition (Name, Definition, Visual, Abilities, LevelUpData)
no entity carries it in a change-appearance session, where the client's pending copy is ecl::character_creation::ChangeAppearanceDefinitionComponent instead

questions.ask: Which function composes the message and what the server checks in it; the companion definition has no such component and no window change was found that sends its look
